title: Art Direction Summit: Building a Visual Identity: An Art Direction Framework
abstracted_dimensions: visual identity across artistic creative technical and marketing constraints
key art as one articulation of a larger identity
limitations: Conference overviews summarize practitioner methods and do not expose the complete talks or controlled audience studies.
The sources discuss commercial game production and cannot establish universal anime or regional illustration conventions.
Named games studios and creators remain citation-only and supply no reusable protected design or style token.
Viewer response and market performance remain hypotheses requiring rendered multi-format review.
reuse_note: Abstract only portable art-direction and single-image storytelling mechanisms. Do not copy named-game compositions, character designs, logos, palettes, title treatments, or artist signatures.

mechanisms.statement: key art articulates previously established art pillars instead of inventing a disconnected decorative finish
a repeatable visual signature coordinates color typography iconography logo and graphic elements across key art and adjacent media
one image can carry a specific narrative event through character-centered staging dramatic tension and emotional consequence
one dominant product promise and one counterforce create a clearer declaration than several equally weighted spectacle motifs
composition approval can accommodate marketing and stakeholder constraints while preserving the same focal promise
key art is one expression of a wider visual identity and cannot substitute for coherent art direction in the underlying work
campaign variants may change layout and surface treatment while retaining stable identity anchors and the same central promise
protected names designs palettes and artist signatures remain citation context rather than executable prompt candidates

illustration_evidence_definitions.key_art_secondary_force_counterweight: One opposing person force environment or consequence balances the focal subject without becoming a second equal poster premise.
illustration_evidence_definitions.key_art_single_event_state: The image captures one legible before-to-after event state rather than a neutral cast lineup.
illustration_evidence_definitions.key_art_gaze_gesture_route: Gaze hand direction body torque or directional effects route attention from the focal subject toward the stake or consequence.

keep the focal event complete with and without an optional title lockup
review first-read hierarchy at thumbnail size and narrative consequence at native size
recompose per format while preserving identity anchors rather than suffixing one prompt with a new ratio
viewer_implications: the first glance should identify who acts and what opposes them
a second look should reveal one consequence or world-scale clue tied to the same promise
coherent signature decisions may support recognition but do not prove brand recall

compatibility: combine one primary subject anchor with one secondary force and one visible consequence
combine a stable visual-signature relation with different campaign layouts rather than repeating the same pose
pair a title-safe region with a focal route that remains complete when no title is present
pair world scale with a specific character action so spectacle does not erase agency
preserve one campaign identity anchor across wide vertical and square adaptations

do not use surface polish or genre labels as substitutes for a visible event and stake
do not let title-safe negative space sever the action-to-consequence route
do not derive a new prompt from a named game's protected composition costume emblem or palette
do not claim market impact or viewer emotion from a prompt audit alone

mechanisms.statement: vertical scrolling foregrounds temporal continuity rather than the simultaneous spatial arrangement of a printed page
scroll distance and gutter density can shape reader-controlled experiential time between narrative beats
continuous vertical panel expansion can combine spatial depth temporal delay emotional intensification and complex information

immersion empathy and emotional intensification remain response hypotheses that require pixel-level sequence review without prompt metadata
